questions.qtext: Prying forces are the additional

options.text: shearing forces on the bolts because of long joint
bending forces on the bolts because of long joint
forces due to friction between the connected parts
tensile forces due to the flexibility of connected parts leading to deformations.

questions.solution:
(d)
Prying forces are additional tensile stresses that develop in bolts when the connected components
are not perfectly rigid and flex under load, causing the bolts to experience increased tension
beyond the initial preload.

questions.qtext: Consider the following statements regarding lacing bars used in a built-up column. Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.text: The purpose of lacing is to hold the various parts of a column straight, parallel, at a correct distance apart and to equalize the stress distribution between its various parts.
The angle of inclination of the lacing bar with the longitudinal axis of the component member is kept between 40° to 70°.
The maximum spacing of lacing bars 'C' should be such that the minimum slenderness ratio of the component member is not greater than 50 or 0.6 times the slenderness ratio of the member as a whole.
For a compression member consisting of two parallel planes of lacing, each lacing is subjected to a transverse shear equal to 1.25% of the axial force in the column.

questions.solution:
(a, b, d)
The maximum spacing of lacing bars ‘C‘ should be such that the minimum slenderness ratio of the
component member is not greater than 50 or 0.7 times the slenderness ratio of the member as a
whole.
